NEW DELHI: The 31st edition of Gifts World Expo and the inaugural Paperworld Delhi will be held together at Bharat Mandapam from July 30 to August 1, bringing the gifting, stationery, paper and office-supplies industries onto a common business platform.The organisers said the co-located exhibitions will feature more than 850 exhibitors, 6,000 brands and around 30,000 products. The events are expected to attract manufacturers, importers, wholesalers, retailers, e-commerce companies, corporate buyers, educational institutions and hospitality-sector purchasers.Gifts World Expo will showcase corporate, festive, wedding, luxury, customised and promotional gifts, besides handicrafts, home décor, travel accessories, kitchen appliances, wellness products and confectionery.Paperworld Delhi, being held in the Capital for the first time after five editions in Mumbai, will focus on stationery, writing instruments, school and office supplies, art materials, paper products, packaging, educational solutions and workplace essentials.The exhibitions will also have dedicated spaces for start-ups, product innovations and sustainable solutions. Industry discussions and workshops under “Gift Talks” and “Paper Talks” will cover consumer trends, branding, packaging, sustainability, retail transformation and changes in workplaces and education.Himani Gulati, director of MEX Exhibitions, said the addition of Paperworld would create opportunities for businesses from the two related industries to engage with a wider group of buyers and suppliers.The exhibitions are being jointly organised by MEX Exhibitions and Messe Frankfurt Trade Fairs India. Organisers said the partnership was aimed at developing an integrated sourcing and networking platform for the gifting and stationery sectors in north India.
Article Summary: The 31st edition of Gifts World Expo and the inaugural Paperworld Delhi will be held together at Bharat Mandapam from July 30 to August 1. The co-located exhibitions will feature more than 850 exhibitors, 6,000 brands and around 30,000 products.

Article Title: Supreme Court relaxes order mandating Coalgate appeals only before itself, allows Delhi high court to hear them
Article Text:
Apex court on Coalgate case

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Diluting its 12year-old order mandating appeals to be filed only in the Supreme Court against trial court orders in coal block allotment scam cases, the SC Wednesday said the prosecution and accused can move the Delhi HC challenging acquittals or convictions recorded by the special judge.Taking up the long pending appeals in coal scam cases, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, “Why did the Supreme Court invite such a burden on itself ? There may have been certain concerns at some point of time. But can the Supreme Court denude the high court’s constitutionally conferred powers to hear appeals against trial court orders? Powers of the high court to hear appeals against trial court is part of the basic structure. ”Appearing for some of the accused in coal scam cases, senior advocate Kapil Sibal said SC should not be the first forum of appeal against trial court orders. However, SC-appointed special public prosecutor R S Cheema said trials in two-thirds of the cases have been over and that the restraint on approaching the high court against interim orders of the special judge should continue.The bench agreed with Cheema but said that in those cases where the trial court has recorded either conviction or acquittal, the appeal by person or prosecution must challenge it before the Delhi high court.In Sept 2014, Supreme Court had cancelled 204 of the 218 coal block allocations and directed that all appeals against framing of charge, quashing of case and bail petitions must be filed only before the Supreme Court and not Delhi high court.This restriction was imposed to prevent accused from delaying trials.Sibal, who was a minister in the Congress-headed UPA govt when the coal scam and 2G scam cases rocked its electoral support base, told the court that the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) had made an omnibus calculation about alleged loss to exchequer because of the coal block allocations, without quantifying loss attributable to individual coal blocks.“We have challenged the basis on which such calculations were made by the CAG. Moreover, we have also questioned whether mere allotment of coal blocks would amount to corrupt practice without any mining having taken place at all,” Sibal said.The top court asked Cheema and the counsel for accused to help in categorizing the bunch of cases for hearing from Aug 18.
Article Summary: Supreme Court says prosecution and accused can move the Delhi HC challenging acquittals or convictions recorded by the special judge. In Sept 2014, Supreme Court had cancelled 204 of the 218 coal block allocations and directed that all appeals against framing of charge, quashing of case and bail petitions must be filed only before the Supreme Court.

Article Title: Automakers silent on E20 petrol due to government pressure: Kejriwal

NEW DELHI: AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal Wednesday alleged that Centre was pressuring automobile manufacturers to remain silent on the impact of E20 petrol on vehicles manufactured before 2023, a charge rejected by Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra, who challenged him to produce evidence of vehicles damaged due to ethanol-blended fuel.Addressing a news conference, Kejriwal said he had written to 29 companies manufacturing two-wheelers and four-wheelers asking whether E20 petrol could be safely used in vehicles manufactured before 2023, and whether they would compensate consumers if such vehicles suffered damage or lower fuel efficiency.He claimed none of the companies responded in writing, but officials from nine companies spoke to him on the phone. Quoting those officials, Kejriwal alleged that using E20 in vehicles manufactured before 2023 could damage the engine and fuel system and reduce fuel efficiency.He further alleged that Centre had warned automobile companies against making such claims publicly, saying their plants could face action by agencies such as ED, CBI and income tax department.He claimed that companies were being pressured to certify that E20 petrol was safe, but Nitin Gadkari and Arvind Kejriwal were reluctant to do so as consumers could seek compensation or replacement of vehicles if damaged, and that Centre’s decision to impose E20 petrol would turn nearly 30 crore pre-2023 vehicles into scrap.Hitting back, Delhi BJP chief Harsh Malhotra said “I again challenge Arvind Kejriwal...to publicly bring forward 100 vehicles with mechanic certification that the vehicle has been damaged due to ethanol mixed petrol.”

Article Title: Over 1 lakh schools in India functioning with a single teacher
Article Text:
File photo

The single-teacher-school data indicates that favourable national averages continue to conceal sharp local imbalances in teacher availability

‘Vacancies due to retirement, resignations, enrolment change’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: More than one lakh schools — government, government-aided and private — are functioning with a single teacher, with Andhra Pradesh alone accounting for over 16,000, government data has revealed, highlighting severe deployment gaps despite the country’s overall pupil-teacher ratio remaining within national norms.The education ministry cited national pupil-teacher ratios of 19 at primary level, 17 at upper primary, 15 at secondary and 23 at higher secondary — all within the limits envisaged under National Education Policy. However, the single-teacher-school data indicates that favourable national averages continue to conceal sharp local imbalances in teacher availability.According to UDISE+ data for 2025-26, India has 1,00,843 single-teacher schools across all management categories. Andhra Pradesh tops the list with 16,357 such schools — more than 16% of the national total — followed by Jharkhand (9,827) and Maharashtra (9,269). Karnataka has 8,042 single-teacher schools, UP 7,874, Rajasthan 7,200 and West Bengal 6,769. Together, these seven states account for nearly 65% of all schools operating with one teacher.The problem is spread across regions rather than being confined to poorer or geographically difficult states.Telangana has 4,793 such schools, Tamil Nadu 3,957 and Assam 3,159. Himachal Pradesh has 3,128, Uttarakhand 2,655 and Chhattisgarh 2,461. At the other end, Kerala reported 67 singleteacher schools, Nagaland 35, Sikkim 31, Ladakh 28, Delhi seven and Andaman and Nicobar Islands one.The figures were provided by MoS for education Jayant Chaudhary in response to a RS question on teacher vacancies. While the question sought data specifically for government schools, the annexure on single-teacher institutions covers schools under all managements.The ministry did not provide state-wise sanctioned posts or vacancies, saying recruitment, service conditions and deployment of teachers were handled by state governments and UT administrations. It attributed vacancies to retirement, resignation, creation of posts, staff rationalisation and changing enrolment, including in rural, tribal and aspirational districts.Government said states were regularly advised to fill posts through transparent, merit-based recruitment and use technology for forecasting teacher requirements. Financial support was also provided under Samagra Shiksha to maintain prescribed pupil-teacher ratios.
Article Summary: Andhra Pradesh tops the list with 16,357 such schools. Karnataka has 8,042 single-teacher schools, UP 7,874, Rajasthan 7,200 and West Bengal 6,769. Telangana has 4,793 such schools, Tamil Nadu 3,957 and Assam 3,159.

Article Title: 'Modiji clocked it': BJP MP's Gen Z-style praise for PM during anti-paper leak Bill debate
Article Text:
BJP MP's Gen Z-style praise for PM during anti-paper leak Bill debate

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party Lok Sabha member Bansuri Swaraj on Tuesday used a Gen Z term to praise the steps taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi against the paper leak. She said that the PM had "clocked it" with the anti-paper leak Bill, a term used by the younger generation to recognize a fact.Speaking in favour of the Bill during the debate, she said, "Borrowing Gen Z's language, I would have to say that Modiji clocked it at providing this legislative solution"."I am standing in support of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. This is a transformative amendment. Its necessity is not only evident, but it is also the demand of the present time. Bringing this amendment is proof of the sensitivity of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his committed government. Speaker Sir, when a competitive examination is compromised, its impact is not limited to the candidate whose future is put at stake," she added.The government has proposed amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act to ensure time-bound investigations, speedy trials and tougher penalties for paper leaks and organised exam fraud.Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced on Sunday the formation of a high-powered task force, headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani, to overhaul India's examination system and make it more transparent, reliable and technology-driven.Addressing students through a video message, PM Modi said the Centre had already taken steps to curb exam malpractice by jailing those involved, setting up fast-track courts and proposing stricter legal provisions, but stressed that broader systemic reforms were now needed.He said the task force would recommend measures to strengthen the credibility of public examinations, with the government acting on its report at the earliest. The Nilekani-led panel will study the use of technology and suggest reforms to improve transparency, efficiency and trust in the conduct of public examinations.The move comes in the wake of recent controversies surrounding competitive examinations, including the NEET row, as the Centre seeks to restore confidence in the system.
Article Summary: Bansuri Swaraj used a Gen Z term to praise the steps taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. She said that the PM had "clocked it" with the anti-paper leak Bill. The government has proposed amendments to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act.

Article Title: 2 years after death, Supreme Court clears former PM Manmohan Singh in Coalgate case
Article Text:
File photo: Former PM Manmohan Singh

NEW DELHI: More than 11 years after a Delhi court sensationally summoned former PM Manmohan Singh as an accused in a coal block allotment scam case, the Supreme Court Wednesday gave him a clean chit, closing the case nearly two years after his demise.Special judge Bharat Parashar, presiding over trials in coal block allotment scam cases which were investigated by the CBI under the SC’s monitoring, had on March 11, 2015, issued summons to Singh in the case relating to irregular allocation of Talabira-II coal block in Odisha to Kumar Mangalam Birla-owned Hindalco. Singh held the charge of coal ministry at the time of the allocation in question.Parashar, now the secretary general of SC, had declined to close the cases despite the CBI filing two successive reports — on Aug 27, 2014, and Oct 21, 2014 — recommending the same.Since the Supreme Court had barred Delhi HC from entertaining appeals against interim orders of the special judge, Singh moved SC challenging trial court’s order.A bench of Justices V Gopala Gowda and C Nagappan had on April 1, 2015, stayed the summoning order, saving the ex-PM the embarrassment of appearing as an accused in the Patiala House Court complex.On Wednesday, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, who had earlier successfully argued in SC for staying the proceedings against Singh, told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalaya Bagchi and V Mohana that though the proceedings would abate due to Singh’s demise in Nov 2024, the court should remove the trial court’s observations against the ex-PM in the summoning order.Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi joined Sibal to reiterate the request.Both the special public prosecutor and senior advocate R S Cheema and additional solicitor general S V Raju had recused themselves, leaving the court with the task of perusing the CBI closure reports on its own before passing the order.The CJI-led bench said the demise of an accused would ordinarily result in the abatement of case against him. After perusing the closure reports, it allowed Singh’s appeal and quashed the trial court’s order taking cognisance of the crime and issuing summons to Singh.
Article Summary: A Delhi court sensationally summoned former PM Manmohan Singh as an accused in a coal block allotment scam case. The Supreme Court Wednesday gave him a clean chit, closing the case nearly two years after his demise. Singh held the charge of coal ministry at the time of the allocation in question.

LUCKNOW: IIT Bombay alumnus Jagdish Aphale has been appointed Ayodhya Ram temple trust’s first secretary and made a joint signatory to financial transactions as the organisation seeks to infuse accountability into its functioning and ride out the storm triggered by alleged theft of donations to the shrine.“For banking purposes, the joint signatories are me and Aphale. He has been privy to the trust’s internal processes over the past fortnight as part of his integration.His name was proposed at the trust’s July 6 meeting, held soon after it accepted the resignations of former general secretary Champat Rai and member Anil Mishra.

Article Title: Delhi high court refuses HPV shots stay, but seeks Centre's response
Article Text:
File photo: Delhi high court

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court on Wednesday refused to stay the HPV (human papillomavirus) immunisation campaign but asked the Centre, Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation, and Indian Council of Medical Research to file separate replies in four weeks on the "justification for introducing the vaccine".It was hearing a PIL that sought a direction to the authorities to review the decision to include HPV vaccines in "Universal Immunisation Programme and raised concerns over their long-term safety, lack of informed consent and monitoring of adverse events."Half-baked vaccines should not be administered. We are only to ensure that the necessary protocol is followed," said the high court.The PIL also sought direction to authorities to conduct and publish district-wise and state-wise evaluations before further expansion. The high court scheduled the next hearing for October 29.
Article Summary: Delhi high court refused to stay the HPV (human papillomavirus) immunisation campaign. It asked the Centre, Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation, and Indian Council of Medical Research to file separate replies in four weeks. It was hearing a PIL that sought a direction to the authorities to review the decision.

Article Title: Now, just one visit for NEET-UG counselling
Article Text:
JP Nadda reviews preparedness for NEET UG counselling 2026

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a major reform, the Centre has introduced one-time physical reporting for NEET-UG counselling, ending repeated visits to allotted medical colleges for candidates seeking a seat upgrade.Aspirants allotted a seat in the first or second round can now complete subsequent reporting and document verification online while retaining their seat for further rounds.Under the new framework, candidates opting for the “Float” option can complete document verification online and receive provisional admission while retaining their allotted seat for subsequent rounds. If allotted a better seat, the earlier one will automatically be released to another candidateThose choosing the “Freeze” option, or retaining a seat after the third round, must report physically to complete admission formalities, including verification of original documents and payment of fees.The reforms were reviewed by Union health minister J P Nadda on Wednesday ahead of the start of NEETUG counselling.“Earlier, every candidate allotted a seat had to physically report to the college even if they wanted to participate in the next round for a better option,” said Dr B Srinivas, deputy director general (medical education), ministry of health and family welfare.“Now, they can complete document verification online, retain the allotted seat and continue in the counselling process.If they get a better seat, the earlier one will be released to another candidate. If not, they will retain their original seat.”The Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) has also introduced online resignation, allowing eligible candidates to surrender their allotted seat through the counselling portal instead of visiting the institute. Another major change is the complete digitisation of admissions under the NRI category.Candidates requiring additional eligibility documents will now upload them through a dedicated portal instead of sending them by email. “Earlier, these documents sometimes landed in spam folders or were missed, delaying verification. The new software allows direct online verification...” Srinivas said.To improve transparency, the counselling system will use pre-populated candidate data from the National Testing Agency, online document verification, NMC-validated seat matrices and enhanced cybersecurity measures developed with the National Informatics Centre.The Centre has also raised the number of assessment centres for persons with benchmark disabilities (PwBD) from 16 to 61 and introduced an Appellate Disability Assessment Board under revised NMC guidelines.Nadda directed officials to ensure a transparent, meritbased counselling process.
Article Summary: Aspirants allotted a seat in the first or second round can now complete subsequent reporting and document verification online while retaining their seat for further rounds. If allotted a better seat, the earlier one will automatically be released to another candidate. The reforms were reviewed by Union health minister J P Nadda on Wednesday.

Article Title: ADGCA-ordered probe cleared Dreamliner fuel switch: Government
Article Text:
Test found no abnormality in dreamliner fuel switch

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A DGCA-ordered probe by Boeing into the fuel control switch locking mechanism of the B787 Dreamliner has found “no abnormality”, govt told Parliament on Wednesday.The regulator had ordered this repeat examination after the crew operating an AI Dreamliner from London to Bengaluru in Feb had observed an issue with the switch after landing safely and had reported the same.The switches, which control fuel supply to engines, have been under scrutiny after AI 171 crashed within seconds of taking off from Ahmedabad in June 2025 as its engines had run out of fuel. While the incident is still being probed, the locking system of fuel control switches has been probed multiple times since then to ensure safety.Dreamliners operating around the world are still being looked at by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), which is probing the crash. The Dreamliner is the most widely used mid-range wide body aircraft globally.“DGCA, as part of continued airworthiness, directed original equipment manufacturer (OEM) level testing of fuel control switch locking mechanism in Seattle. Detailed examination of fuel control switch including structural integrity of fuel control switch detents was carried out and no abnormality was observed,” minister of state for civil aviation Murlidhar Mohol said in reply to a Parliament question Wednesday.The minister, however, added that “further inspection of complete thrust control module at OEM facility is underway”.This module translates pilot inputs or autothrottle commands into precise electronic signals to control engine power.On Feb 2, 2026, the AI Dreamliner on which the crew had reported an issue with the fuel control switch after landing in Bengaluru had been grounded for checks. At that time, AI had said in a statement: “We are aware that one of our pilots has reported a possible defect on the fuel control switch of a Boeing 787 aircraft...We have grounded the said aircraft and are involving the OEM to get the pilot’s concerns checked on a priority basis. The matter has been communicated to the aviation regulator, DGCA. Air India had checked the fuel control switches on all Boeing 787 aircraft in its fleet after a directive from the DGCA, and had found no issues.”On the AI 171 crash, Mohol said Wednesday: “There is no delay in the investigation. The timeline for a major accident investigation cannot be predicted, as it depends on several factors and is an evolving process. The final report will be made public and published on AAIB’s website after completion.”
Article Summary: DGCA-ordered probe by Boeing into the fuel control switch locking mechanism of the B787 Dreamliner has found “no abnormality” The regulator had ordered this repeat examination after the crew operating an AI Dreamliner from London to Bengaluru in Feb had observed an issue with the switch.

Article Title: Ahead of dengue vaccine rollout, all 4 strains found in circulation
Article Text:
Dengue vaccine rollout (representative image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: As India moves towards introducing a dengue vaccine by next year, the country's first nationwide mapping of dengue virus strains has found all four serotypes circulating simultaneously in eight states and UTs, a development researchers say could influence vaccine strategy as infections with multiple strains are associated with more severe disease.The pan-India molecular surveillance study, led by ICMR-National Institute of Virology, Pune, analysed 6,889 lab-confirmed dengue samples collected through 45 virus research and diagnostic laboratories (VRDLs) across 25 states and UTs between 2023 and 2025. It found that dengue serotypes - at least two - were co-circulating in each state and UT included in the surveillance, indicating increasing hyperendemicity of the disease in India.According to the study, all four dengue serotypes (DENV-1, DENV-2, DENV-3 and DENV-4) were detected simultaneously in Andhra, Gujarat, Haryana, MP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal. Fifteen other states and UTs had three serotypes in circulation, while two reported circulation of two serotypes.Researchers found DENV-2 to be the dominant circulating strain, accounting for 51% of infections, followed by DENV-3 (13%), DENV-1 (7%) and DENV-4 (1%).About 7% of patients were infected with two or more dengue serotypes simultaneously.The study found patients with concurrent infections were more likely to develop thrombocytopenia, haemorrhagic manifestations and arthralgia than those infected with a single serotype, suggesting that circulation of multiple strains could increase the burden of severe dengue.The researchers said continuous molecular surveillance is essential to monitor changing dengue virus circulation, improve outbreak prediction and guide vaccine introduction strategies. They noted that several dengue vaccine candidates are in advanced stages of development and that vaccine efficacy varies against different serotypes, making surveillance critical for immunisation policy.The study also highlighted regional differences in virus circulation. While DENV-2 predominated across India, DENV-1 accounted for a relatively larger share of infections in Tamil Nadu (29%), Haryana (38%) and Rajasthan (25%). DENV-3 was more frequently detected in Gujarat (30%), TN(29%), UP (29%) and WB (20%).
Article Summary: India's first nationwide mapping of dengue virus strains has found all four serotypes circulating simultaneously in eight states and UTs. Article Title: Supreme Court bars government from post facto green clearance to projects
Article Text:
File photo

Supreme Court: Follow 2006 notification for prior EC nod

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Wednesday saved central and state projects worth Rs 20,000 crore from demolition for want of prior environmental clearance but permanently prohibited govt from granting post facto EC and quashed Centre’s 2021 Office Memorandum for keeping a window indefinitely open for projects to seek such green nods.Rescinding a part of its earlier decision that had quashed Centre’s 2017 notification, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul M Pancholi said the 2017 notification was valid as it had a limited period window for clearance to projects of significant public interest.However, the bench concurred with the earlier decision to quash the 2021 OM as finding it to be an open-ended administrative order was tantamount to a perpetual amnesty regime for grant of EC to projects undertaken without prior green nod. It said the OM was without having any rational nexus with public interest, and hence is in breach of Environment Protection Act, 1986.Supreme Court said its judgment will operate prospectively, and the ECs granted to various projects under the 2017 notification and the 2021 OM would remain valid. “The prior EC regime under the 2006 notification is mandatory and unless amended by an appropriate notification, would not accommodate grant of post facto EC or retention of projects where constructions have commenced or processes begun without a valid EC,” it said.Supreme Court directed scrupulous adherence to the 2006 notification mandating prior EC clearance for projects. The bench said, “Govt is restrained from issuing administrative orders in future for grant of EC in respect of projects which have commenced in contravention of the prior EC regime under the 2006 notification.”Pending applications (for grant of post facto EC) shall be dealt with in accordance with the law, it said, adding that “no fresh application for grant of EC under the aforesaid instruments (2014 notification or 2021 OM) shall be entertained.”Writing the judgment, Justice Bagchi said the court aimed to strike a balance between an “existential right of all living beings both present and future to a pollution-free environment and an aspirational right to development of a sixth of the world’s population”.The bench, however, noted that Centre has powers under Jan Vishwas Act to decriminalise violations of EP Act by notifying amnesty schemes with regard to such classes or categories of non-compliant projects whose sustainability is necessary to subserve larger public interest.In Nov last year, a bench of then CJI B R Gavai and Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and K Vinod Chandran by two to one majority decided to review the court’s May 2025 decision by Justices A S Oka and Bhuyan which had quashed all post facto green clearance which left public projects worth Rs 20,000 crore vulnerable to demolition.
Article Summary: Supreme Court quashes Centre’s 2021 Office Memorandum for keeping a window indefinitely open for projects to seek green nods. It said the OM was without having any rational nexus with public interest, and hence is in breach of Environment Protection Act, 1986.

Article Title: No ban on Jagannath movie, artists must enjoy creative liberty, says Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: Rejecting a plea seeking a ban on release of an animated film on Mahaprabhu Jagannath, Supreme Court on Wednesday said artists must enjoy the liberty of creative expression, with courts not getting in the way of art and creativity.As Jagannath temple committee strongly opposed the release of the animation film, a bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan said that if depiction of gods and goddesses is prevented, then movies on the Ramayana and Mahabharata would not be made and screened at all. It stressed that people ought to be tolerant of depiction of gods and goddesses."If this is the kind of sensibility, sensitivity...we will pass an order that in respect of Hindu God, Goddess or Mythology, let there be no art form in India! We have Kabir's Ramayana, Valmiki Ramayana, Skanda Ramayana, etc. We have Ramayana in every State. Every person has his own creativity. If we pass such an order, all Ramayana, Mahabharata on television will stop! No art in any form, television, creativity, painting, sculpture of Hindu God or Goddess. .." Supreme Court said.Bench said that when the film was passed by Censor Board then there was no reason for the court to interfere and people should not object to the screening of a film which had been approved by the statutory body."Just because there are two-three sensitive people, can we pass an extreme order that with respect to deity, there shall be no creativity, no literature, no sculpture?...Animated films are for the purpose of children...Earlier, there used to be Yashodhama every night. People used to collect money for it. Artists can't be taken to ransom like this," court said while rejecting the plea of the temple committee."We cannot sit in judgement in the matter of art and creativity," it said.Advocate general of Odisha Pritambar Acharya submitted that Lord Jagannath cannot be depicted as Doraemon and Spiderman. But senior advocate Devadatt Kamat, appearing for the producer, refuted the allegation that the deity had been shown in a derogatory manner and pointed out that committee members had walked out of the special screening of the film.The court thereafter refused to modify its earlier order allowing release of the film.
Article Summary: Supreme Court rejects a plea seeking a ban on release of an animated film on Mahaprabhu Jagannath. Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan said that if depiction of gods and goddesses is prevented, then movies on the Ramayana and Mahabharata would not be made.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In a move aimed at reducing the compliance burden and improving ease of doing business for vehicle manufacturers, the road transport ministry has proposed changes to the conformity of production (CoP) regime for emission compliance for new and existing vehicle models.Under the draft proposal, the CoP test for emission compliance of new models of passenger cars and two-wheelers will be conducted annually for the first three years after type approval and thereafter once every three years. For larger passenger vehicles, goods vehicles and heavy commercial vehicles, the CoP test will continue to be conducted annually.For existing models, the testing frequency will be reduced to once every three years for two-wheelers, passenger cars, larger passenger vehicles, goods vehicles and heavy commercial vehicles.At present, the CoP test for all passenger car models is conducted annually, while for two-wheelers—which are produced in much larger volumes—the testing frequency ranges from once every three months to once a year, depending on production volume.CoP is a regulatory verification process that ensures mass-produced vehicles continue to conform to their original type-approval specifications.“The proposed policy delinks the CoP testing frequency from the volume of vehicles produced or imported. Manufacturers and importers will need to strengthen their quality control systems and ensure continued compliance with the norms, as any defect or deviation detected after three years could expose them to the risk of recalling a large number of vehicles, particularly two-wheelers,” an official said.Under the CoP regime, testing agencies randomly pick vehicles from assembly lines, dealerships or the open market for emission compliance tests, with the entire cost of testing being borne by vehicle manufacturers.
Article Summary: The road transport ministry has proposed changes to the conformity of production (CoP) regime. CoP is a regulatory verification process that ensures mass- produced vehicles continue to conform to their original type-approval specifications. At present, the CoP test for all passenger car models is conducted annually.

Authorities deployed heavy security at Roshanpura Square, where the farmers camped while negotiations continued at the state secretariat.Although repeated scuffles broke out between protesters and police and the windows of a few buses were damaged, police did not resort to force.The farmers are demanding procurement of the entire summer moong crop at MSP, the scrapping of the e-token system for fertiliser distribution and timely availability of fertilisers ahead of the next sowing season.In an attempt to resolve the standoff, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav announced the formation of a four-member committee to hold discussions with farmer representatives."The government has always stood with farmers and is ready to consider positive suggestions. At the same time, both sides should ensure that the public doesn’t face inconvenience. Under PM-AASHA guidelines, procurement is allowed up to 25 per cent of estimated production, with any procurement beyond that limit to be undertaken by the state government.According to data available with the Centre until July 29, Madhya Pradesh had procured around 60,000 tonnes of summer moong so far, Chouhan said, urging the state government to speed up procurement in the interest of farmers.

Article Title: Use of maize & rice for ethanol production sees huge jump
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: While the use of rice, maize and damaged food grain for ethanol manufacturing has increased manifold in the past six years, maize has surpassed rice sold by Food Corporation of India (FCI) to distilleries under govt’s ethanol blended petrol (EBP) programme.Food ministry’s data submitted to Lok Sabha on Wednesday show that till June end of the current 2025-26 ethanol supply year (Oct to Sept), a little over 54 lakh tonne of FCI’s surplus rice and damaged foodgrain (including broken rice) had been used by distilleries under EBP programme, while the figure for maize was around 68 lakh tonne. Two months of the current ethanol supply year (ESY) are still left.Data show that there was no use of maize for ethanol manufacturing during ESY of 2020-21 and 2021-22. After a modest start in ESY 2022-23 with 8.3 lakh tonne of maize being used for manufacturing the bio-fuel, the figure jumped to 75.4 lakh tonne the next year and 131 lakh tonne in ESY 2024-25, which was an all-time high. In comparison, a little over 50 lakh tonne of FCI’s surplus rice and broken rice was used for ethanol production in 2024-25.The ministry said, “Diversification of feedstock base for ethanol production to sugarcane juice, B-heavy molasses, C-heavy molasses, maize, damaged food grains, surplus FCI rice has reduced dependence on any single feedstock or crop and has supported agricultural diversification.”It added that inclusion of maize as a feedstock for ethanol production has helped provide farmers with assured markets and ensured better prices.FCI sells surplus rice for ethanol production after meeting the requirements under National Food Security Act and other welfare schemes and maintaining a buffer stock, the ministry stated. FCI had stopped supply of rice for ethanol production during ESY 2022-23.As per sugar industry, only 2,890 million litres of ethanol, just 28% of the total requirement, are to be procured from sugar-based feedstocks for ESY 2025–26, compared to 72% or 7,610 million litres from grain-based sources, of which 4,780 million litres are from maize (45%), and 2,830 million litres from rice (22%).On Tuesday, govt informed Rajya Sabha that FCI had sold rice to ethanol distilleries at Rs 2,250-2,320 per quintal during June 2025–June 2026, about 40% below its acquisition cost of Rs 3,720-3,889 a quintal. FCI’s average acquisition cost includes MSP and storage and carrying costs.

Article Title: 'No abnormality found in AI Dreamliner fuel control switch locking mechanism': Govt
Article Text:
The switches — which control fuel supply to engines — have been under scrutiny following AI 171 which crashed within seconds of taking off from Ahmedabad last June.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A DGCA-ordered probe by Boeing into the fuel control switch locking mechanism of the B787 Dreamliner has found “no abnormality” with the same, govt told Parliament Wednesday. The regulator had ordered this repeat examination following the crew operating an AI Dreamliner (VT-ANX) from London to Bengaluru this Feb had observed an issue with the switch after landing safely and had reported the same.These switches — which control fuel supply to engines — have been under scrutiny following AI 171 which crashed within seconds of taking off from Ahmedabad last June as its engines had run out of fuel. While why that happened is still being probed, the locking system of fuel control switches has been probed multiple times since then to ensure safety on other Dreamliners operating around the world and are still being looked at by Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) which is probing AI 171 crash. The Dreamliner is the most widely used mid-range wide body aircraft globally.“DGCA, as part of continued airworthiness, directed original equipment manufacturer (OEM) level testing of fuel control switch locking mechanism in Seattle.Detailed examination of fuel control switch including structural integrity of fuel control switch detents was carried out and no abnormality was observed,” Union minister of state for aviation Murlidhar Mohol said in a parliamentary reply Wednesday.However, the minister added that “further inspection of complete thrust control module at OEM facility is underway”. This module translates pilot inputs or autothrottle commands into precise electronic signals to control engine power.On Feb 2, 2026, the AI Dreamliner on which the crew had reported an issue with the fuel control switch after landing in Bengaluru had been grounded for checks. At that time AI had said in a statement: “We are aware that one of our pilots has reported a possible defect on the fuel control switch of a Boeing 787-8 aircraft. After receiving this initial information, we have grounded the said aircraft and are involving the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) to get the pilot’s concerns checked on a priority basis. The matter has been communicated to the aviation regulator, DGCA. Air India had checked the fuel control switches on all Boeing 787 aircraft in its fleet after a directive from the DGCA, and had found no issues.”The AI 171 crash preliminary investigation report of the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau had said: “In the cockpit voice recording, one of the pilots is heard asking the other why did he cutoff (the fuel control switch).The other pilot responded that he did not do so,” says.Meanwhile, on Wednesday about the AI 171 crash probe Mohol said: “There is no delay in the investigation. The timeline for a major accident investigation cannot be predicted, as it depends on several factors and is an evolving process involving multiple variables. The investigation is under progress. All probable causes and contributing factors leading to the accident are being investigated. The final investigation report (including all the findings) will be made public and published on. AAIB website after completion of the investigation.”
Article Summary: The regulator had ordered this repeat examination following the crew operating an AI Dreamliner (VT-ANX) from London to Bengaluru this Feb had observed an issue with the switch. The switches — which control fuel supply to engines — have been under scrutiny following AI 171 which crashed within seconds of taking off from Ahmedabad last June.

CHENNAI: A report released by the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) and the National Election Watch (NEW) has revealed that nearly half of the country's chief ministers face criminal cases. According to the findings, 14 (45%) of the 31 chief ministers, nearly half of them, have declared criminal cases against themselves.More concerning is that 11 chief ministers (35%), one-third of them, face serious criminal charges, including offences carrying maximum punishments of five years or more, non-bailable cognizable offences, assault, murder, kidnapping, crimes against women, and violations under the Prevention of Corruption Act. Notably, two chief ministers have declared cases related to 'attempt to murder'.The average assets per chief minister stand at a staggering Rs 118.07 crore. Out of the 31 chief ministers analysed, four (13%) are billionaires with declared assets crossing Rs 100 crore.Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar tops the list as the wealthiest, with total assets exceeding Rs 1,413 crore, followed by Andhra Pradesh chief minister Chandrababu Naidu (Rs 931 crores+), Tamil Nadu's C Joseph Vijay (Rs 648 crores+), and Arunachal Pradesh's Pema Khandu (Rs 332 crores+).The average assets per chief minister stand at a staggering Rs 118.07 crore. Out of the 31 chief ministers analysed, four (13%) are billionaires with declared assets crossing Rs 100 crore. At the other end of the spectrum, Jammu and Kashmir's Omar Abdullah declared the lowest assets at Rs 55.24 lakhs, followed by West Bengal's Suvendu Adhikari (Rs 85.87 lakh) and Rajasthan's Bhajan Lal Sharma (Rs 1.46 crore). Out of the 31 chief ministers evaluated, Rekha Gupta (Delhi) is the sole woman chief minister.Majority of chief ministers are well-educated. Postgraduates form the largest segment at 29% (nine), followed by graduates at 23% (seven), graduate professionals at 19% (six), doctorates at 10% (three), and Class 10 or 12 pass accounting for the remainder.The analysis based on self-sworn affidavits filed by all 31 incumbent chief ministers before contesting their respective last elections has brought to light striking details regarding their criminal backgrounds, financial status and education across India's 28 states and 3 Union territories. Article Title: SC grants bail to two alleged Indian Mujahideen operatives after 12 years
Article Text:
Supreme Court grants bail to two accused of operating under Indian Mujahideen (ANI image)

Court notes overlapping FIRs

Bail subject to conditions

Background of the case

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has granted bail to two alleged Indian Mujahideen operatives who have been in custody since 2014, holding that their prolonged incarceration without the trial nearing completion was a violation of their fundamental right to liberty under Article 21 of the Constitution.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta granted relief to Mohd Saquib Ansari and Waqar Azhar, who had challenged an April order of the Delhi high court rejecting their bail pleas in a terror case registered by the Delhi Police Special Cell in November 2011.In its July 27 order, the apex court observed that the two accused had spent nearly 12 years in custody with little progress in the trial."...we feel that the continued incarceration of the petitioners in this case is grossly violative of the right to liberty enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India," the Bench said.The court also noted that the trial had progressed at an extremely slow pace and there was no immediate prospect of its conclusion. It further pointed out that one of the co-accused had already been granted bail.The Bench observed that the petitioners had been arrested in connection with three FIRs, including two registered in Rajasthan, and had remained in custody since 2014.It said the allegations in the three cases substantially overlapped."Having appreciated the submissions advanced at bar and upon going through the record, we find that the petitioners have, more or less, been implicated in three separate FIRs for overlapping allegations," the court said.The court directed that Ansari and Azhar be released on bail in connection with the Delhi case on terms and conditions to be decided by the trial court, provided they are not required in any other case.The Bench directed the accused to continue cooperating with the trial and said the prosecution would be free to approach the Supreme Court if they attempted to delay proceedings, failed to cooperate or misused the liberty granted to them.The court also clarified that its observations were limited to deciding the bail applications and should not be treated as comments on the merits of the case.Ansari and Azhar had challenged the Delhi high court's April 24 order rejecting their bail pleas after the trial court had also denied them relief.While refusing bail, the high court observed that the two were active members of the banned terrorist organisation Indian Mujahideen and key operatives of its Rajasthan module. It also noted that they allegedly had links with the outfit's leadership in both India and Pakistan.The duo was arrested by the Delhi Police Special Cell in March 2014 and booked under provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
Article Summary: Supreme Court grants bail to two accused of operating under Indian Mujahideen. Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta granted relief to Mohd Saquib Ansari and Waqar Azhar. They had challenged an April order of the Delhi high court rejecting their bail pleas.

Article Title: Karnataka bags lion’s share of electronics startup fund; 90 of 128 firms based in state
Article Text:
Karnataka bags lion’s share of electronics startup fund; 90 of 128 firms based in state

NEW DELHI: Karnataka has emerged as the biggest beneficiary of the Centre’s Electronics Development Fund (EDF), accounting for 90 of the 128 companies backed under the scheme and nearly two-thirds of the total investment made by its associated venture funds.The eight “daughter funds” supported by EDF invested Rs 1,335.77 crore in 128 startups and companies as of June 30, the electronics and information technology ministry told Lok Sabha on Wednesday. Of these, 77 firms were working in electronics system design and manufacturing and 51 in information technology.Bengaluru alone accounted for 89 companies — 56 in electronics manufacturing and 33 in IT — while one company was based in Belagavi. Together, Karnataka-based firms received Rs 854.54 crore, or about 64% of the total investment.Telangana was a distant second, with seven Hyderabad-based companies receiving Rs 129.97 crore. Eight companies in Mumbai and Pune received Rs 142.48 crore, while six Delhi firms were allotted Rs 99.2 crore. Five Chennai companies received Rs 62.24 crore.The remaining investments went to companies in Haryana, Kerala, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.No company from Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu figured among the beneficiaries, according to the state-wise data submitted in Parliament.EDF was established as a “fund of funds”, with the government investing Rs 257.77 crore in eight professionally managed, Sebi-registered venture funds. These funds subsequently deployed more than five times that amount in technology companies. The supported firms have collectively raised around Rs 22,553.82 crore and created or acquired 373 intellectual-property assets, the ministry said.Companies were selected on the basis of their innovation potential, indigenous technology development, capacity to create intellectual property, the technical strength of their founding teams and the commercial scalability of their business models.Canbank Venture Capital Fund Ltd manages EDF, while the electronics ministry is its anchor investor. The fund completed its investment phase in February 2024 and is now in the divestment phase. Its daughter funds continue to monitor the operational performance, market growth and technological progress of the companies they backed.
Article Summary: Karnataka has emerged as the biggest beneficiary of the Centre’s Electronics Development Fund. Bengaluru alone accounted for 89 companies — 56 in electronics manufacturing and 33 in IT. No company from Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu figured among the beneficiaries.

Article Title: India Stack goes global: DigiLocker work starts in Kenya, Cuba
Article Text: NEW DELHI: India has signed agreements with 24 countries to export its digital public infrastructure model, moving beyond broad cooperation pledges to begin work on DigiLocker systems in Kenya and Cuba and expand UPI-linked payments across 10 overseas markets. Discussions are also underway with Laos, Seychelles, Venezuela, Armenia, Fiji, Guyana and Colombia for possible adoption of platforms such as e-Sanjeevani, e-Office and e-Hospital.The electronics and information technology ministry told Lok Sabha on Wednesday that India had concluded an implementation framework agreement and a non-disclosure agreement with Kenya for deploying DigiLocker. Development of a foundational DigiLocker platform has also begun in Cuba.The agreements provide for capacity building, exchange of technical knowledge and best practices, expert consultations, joint workshops, feasibility studies and pilot projects. The partner countries include Kenya, Cuba, Colombia, Sri Lanka, Brazil, Maldives, Mongolia, Seychelles, Armenia, Fiji, Venezuela, Ethiopia and Tanzania.The overseas push seeks to position India Stack — the ecosystem of interoperable identity, payments, document and service-delivery platforms — as a development tool, particularly for countries in the Global South.India conducted a specialised course on digital public infrastructure for a Cuban delegation in December 2025 under the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation programme. Foreign delegations from Kenya, Rwanda, Nepal, Indonesia and South Africa have also interacted with agencies such as UIDAI, NPCI, the National Informatics Centre and C-DAC.UPI merchant payments are currently available in Bhutan, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Qatar, Singapore, Sri Lanka, the UAE and Cambodia. Cross-border person-to-person payment links are operational with Singapore, Nepal and Greece.Among the latest additions, UPI merchant payments went live in Cambodia in June 2026, while a person-to-person link with Greece became operational in May. Nepal introduced cross-border person-to-person transfers in June, adding to merchant payments available there since March 2024.The government has also approved a Social Impact Fund to provide financial and technical assistance for pilot deployment of digital public infrastructure in low- and middle-income countries.
Article Summary: India has signed agreements with 24 countries to export its digital public infrastructure model. Discussions are also underway with Laos, Seychelles, Venezuela, Armenia, Fiji, Guyana and Colombia for possible adoption of platforms such as e-Sanjeevani, e-Office and e-Hospital.

Article Title: Vande Mataram Bill 2026 explained: What changes and what punishment it proposes
Article Text:
Vande Mataram Bill passed (ANI image on left)

What does the current law say?

What changes does the Bill propose?

Why was the amendment introduced?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Rajya Sabha on Wednesday passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026, paving the way for Vande Mataram to receive the same statutory protection.The amendment is intended to place National Song Vande Mataram on the same legal footing as National Anthem Jana Gana Mana with respect to protection against insult or disruption.During a debate in the Rajya Sabha, MoS for home affairs Nityanand Rai said the amendment was "not merely a legislative change" but reflected the country's commitment to "the soul of India, national consciousness, cultural heritage, and the ideals of the freedom struggle."The Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 currently provides statutory protection to the National Flag, the Constitution of India, and the National Anthem, Jana Gana Mana.Under Section 3of the Act, it is a punishable offence to intentionally prevent the singing of the National Anthem or disturb an assembly engaged in its rendition. Such offences are punishable withimprisonment for up to three years, a fine, or both.The amendment seeks to extend the legal protections currently available to the National Anthem to Vande Mataram. If enacted into law, deliberately insulting the National Song, intentionally preventing its singing, or disrupting an assembly engaged in singing it would become punishable offences.These acts would attract the same penalty as similar offences involving the National Anthem under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971, with punishment of up to three years' imprisonment, a fine, or both.The Rajya Sabha has passed the Bill, but it must complete the remaining constitutional process before becoming law, including any remaining parliamentary approval, if applicable, and receiving the President's assent.The song, composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, played a significant role in India's freedom struggle. At the Constituent Assembly meeting held on January 24, 1950, its President, Dr Rajendra Prasad, stated that Vande Mataram, which had played a historic role in the freedom movement, "shall be honoured equally with Jana Gana Mana" and accorded equal respect, even as Jana Gana Mana was adopted as the national anthem.Despite this recognition, Vande Mataram did not enjoyed the same statutory protection under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971, a gap the proposed amendment seeks to address.The government says the amendment seeks to remove this distinction by extending identical legal safeguards.
Article Summary: The Rajya Sabha on Wednesday passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026. The amendment is intended to place National Song Vande Mataram on the same legal footing as National Anthem Jana Gana Mana with respect to protection against insult or disruption.

Article Title: Bihar transgender welfare board approves proposal to build temple dedicated to PM Modi
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The Bihar State Transgender Welfare Board on Wednesday approved a proposal to construct a temple dedicated to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with a board member saying the prime minister had given the transgender community "respect and rights".The proposal was moved by board member Ranjan Singh during the maiden meeting of the board, which functions under the Bihar government's Social Welfare Department."Since the transgender community in Bihar does not have a temple of its own, I proposed to build a temple for Narendra Modi because he gave us respect and rights. The proposal received the support of all members and was approved by the board," Singh told PTI.The Bihar government constituted the Bihar State Transgender Welfare Board in August last year to safeguard the rights of the transgender community and undertake measures for its social development and empowerment.According to Singh, Wednesday's meeting was the first gathering of the board after the implementation of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019."Today's meeting marked the first gathering of the Bihar State Transgender Welfare Board following the enactment of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019, which provided the transgender community with institutional representation in the state secretariat," Singh said.
Article Summary: The Bihar State Transgender Welfare Board approved a proposal to construct a temple dedicated to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The proposal was moved by board member Ranjan Singh during the maiden meeting of the board. The Bihar government constituted the board in August last year to safeguard the rights of the transgender community.

Article Title: Over 1 lakh schools run with just one teacher; Andhra tops list with 16,357
Article Text: NEW DELHI: More than one lakh schools across India are functioning with a single teacher, with Andhra Pradesh alone accounting for over 16,000, government data has revealed, highlighting severe deployment gaps despite the country’s overall pupil-teacher ratio remaining within national norms.According to UDISE+ data for 2025-26, India has 1,00,843 single-teacher schools across all management categories. Andhra Pradesh tops the list with 16,357 such schools — more than 16% of the national total — followed by Jharkhand with 9,827 and Maharashtra with 9,269.Karnataka has 8,042 single-teacher schools, Uttar Pradesh 7,874, Rajasthan 7,200 and West Bengal 6,769. Together, the seven states account for nearly 65% of all schools in the country operating with only one teacher.The problem is spread across regions rather than being confined to poorer or geographically difficult states. Telangana has 4,793 such schools, Tamil Nadu 3,957 and Assam 3,159. Himachal Pradesh has 3,128, Uttarakhand 2,655 and Chhattisgarh 2,461.At the other end, Kerala reported 67 single-teacher schools, Nagaland 35, Sikkim 31, Ladakh 28, Delhi seven and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands one.The figures were provided by minister of state for education Jayant Chaudhary in response to a Rajya Sabha question on teacher vacancies.While the question sought data specifically for government schools, the annexure on single-teacher institutions covers schools under all managements.The ministry did not provide state-wise sanctioned posts or vacancies, saying recruitment, service conditions and deployment of teachers were handled by state governments and Union Territory administrations. It attributed vacancies to retirement, resignation, creation of posts, staff rationalisation and changing enrolment, including in rural, tribal and aspirational districts.The Centre said states were regularly advised to fill posts through transparent, merit-based recruitment and use technology for forecasting teacher requirements. Financial support was also provided under Samagra Shiksha to maintain prescribed pupil-teacher ratios.The ministry cited national pupil-teacher ratios of 19 at the primary level, 17 at upper primary, 15 at secondary and 23 at higher secondary — all within the limits envisaged under the National Education Policy. However, the single-teacher-school data indicates that favourable national averages continue to conceal sharp local imbalances in teacher availability.
Article Summary: Andhra Pradesh tops the list with 16,357 such schools. Karnataka has 8,042 single-teacher schools, Uttar Pradesh 7,874, Rajasthan 7,200 and West Bengal 6,769. Together, the seven states account for nearly 65% of all schools operating with only one teacher.

Article Title: 'No abnormality found in fuel control switch': Government on Air India Boeing 787 crash
Article Text:
'No abnormality found in fuel control switch': Government on Air India Boeing 787 crash

What the government said about the AI-171 probe

Fuel switches moved to 'CUTOFF' after take-off

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Wednesday said no abnormality has been found in the fuel control switch locking mechanism of the Air India Boeing 787 Dreamliner that crashed shortly after take-off from Ahmedabad on June 12 last year killing 260 people on board and on the ground.Civil aviation state minister Murlidhar Mohol informed the Rajya Sabha that the fuel control switch was examined at the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) level in Seattle as part of continued airworthiness checks ordered by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), Reuters repeorted.A detailed examination of the fuel control switch, including the structural integrity of its locking detents, found 'no abnormality', Mohol said in his response to questions raised by Congress MP Jebi Mather Hisham. However, the examination of the complete thrust control module is still underway at the OEM facility in Seattle."Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), as part of continued airworthiness, directed Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) level testing of Fuel Control Switch Locking Mechanism in Seattle. Detailed examination of Fuel Control Switch including structural integrity of Fuel Control Switch detents was carried out and no abnormality was observed.However, further inspection of complete 'Thrust Control Module' at OEM facility is underway," Mohol write in his written reply.The government also rejected suggestions that the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has delayed its final report into the crash.In her Rajya Sabha question, Mather had asked the government to state the reasons for the delay in releasing the final report more than a year after the crash, whether pilot conduct was among the factors being examined and whether the government would announce a public release date for the complete report.Responding to these questions, Mohol said there was 'no delay' in the investigation and explained that major accident investigations cannot be completed according to a fixed timeline."There is no delay in the investigation. The timeline for a major accident investigation cannot be predicted, as it depends on several factors and is an evolving process involving multiple variables," he said in the written reply.The minister said the investigation remains under way and that all possible causes and contributing factors are being examined."All probable causes and contributing factors leading to the accident are being investigated," Mohol said.The government said the final investigation report, containing all the findings of the probe, would be made public and published on the AAIB website once the investigation is complete.Air India flight AI-171, which was headed to London, crashed shortly after taking off from Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport in Ahmedabad on June 12, 2025.The Boeing 787 struck a medical college hostel complex soon after take-off. The crash killed 241 people on board and 19 people on the ground, while one passenger survived.The disaster became one of India's deadliest aviation accidents in recent years and triggered a detailed investigation into the circumstances surrounding the crash.A preliminary investigation report released last year found that the fuel control switches of both engines moved from 'RUN' to 'CUTOFF' shortly after take-off, cutting the fuel supply and causing both engines to shut down.A cockpit recording also captured a brief exchange between the pilots in which one pilot appeared to ask the other why the switches had been moved, while the other denied doing so. The finding raised questions about whether the switches had been moved by a pilot or whether a technical issue could have been responsible.The government has not provided a specific date for publication of the final AAIB report.Mohol said the investigation was still progressing and that the report would be released only after the inquiry is completed. The government has maintained that the investigation will cover all probable causes and contributing factors.
Article Summary: The fuel control switch was examined at the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) level in Seattle. The crash killed 241 people on board and 19 people on the ground, while one passenger survived. A preliminary investigation report released last year found that the fuel control switches of both engines moved from 'RUN' to 'CUTOFF' shortly after take-off.

Article Title: E20 petrol and vehicle mileage: What Nitin Gadkari said amid growing concerns
Article Text:
Poll Vote & Share your view Should there be more transparency about the effects of E20 fuel on vehicles? Yes, absolutely. No, it's not necessary. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The government on Wednesday said extensive studies have found no significant performance or durability issues in vehicles running on E20 petrol, asserting that even older vehicles generally do not require engine modifications to use the fuel.In a written reply in the Rajya Sabha, road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari said tests found no issues in parameters such as drivability, startability, metal compatibility and plastic compatibility.Responding to concerns over fuel efficiency, Gadkari said automobile manufacturers and vehicle-testing agencies have clarified that mileage depends on several factors and cannot be attributed solely to the type of fuel used.He said a joint study by Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOCL), Indian Institute of Petroleum (IIP), Dehradun, Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), and Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) evaluated the impact of E20 fuel on two-wheelers and four-wheelers."The studies confirmed that even legacy vehicles did not exhibit any significant variations in performance, nor did they show abnormal wear and tear when operated with E20 fuel," Gadkari said.He added that the studies did not indicate any need to modify car or two-wheeler engines for using E20 fuel.Gadkari, however, said that in BS-III vehicles introduced from April 1, 2005, and manufactured before 2016, some rubber parts and gaskets may require replacement. "This can be easily managed during the routine servicing regime of the vehicle," he said.The rollout of E20 petrol, a blend of 80% petrol and 20% ethanol, has faced criticism from opposition parties and some consumer groups over its impact on older vehicles not specifically designed for higher ethanol blends.Critics have questioned vehicle compatibility, raised concerns about reduced fuel efficiency and higher maintenance costs, and sought clarity on liability in case of engine or fuel-system damage.The government has maintained that the transition has been phased and backed by extensive testing, while automobile manufacturers have said they continue to honour warranty claims for vehicles using E20 fuel. Opposition parties have repeatedly sought greater transparency on vehicle compatibility and consumer safeguards.Gadkari said an inter-ministerial committee (IMC), constituted under NITI Aayog on December 26, 2020, comprehensively examined vehicle compatibility and fuel-efficiency aspects of ethanol blending. The assessment was supported by research conducted by IOCL, ARAI and SIAM.The committee's "Roadmap for Ethanol Blending in India 2020-25", released in June 2021, was prepared after extensive consultations with automobile manufacturers, oil marketing companies and agricultural experts. It examined material compatibility, engine calibration, fuel systems, drivability, durability, emissions and fuel efficiency before the introduction of E20 fuel.Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme has been implemented through a phased, calibrated, scientifically validated and consultative approach, Gadkari said.He also noted that ethanol-blended fuel has been used globally for more than a century, with countries such as Brazil using even higher ethanol blends for decades.In India, the EBP Programme began as a pilot project in 2001, and E5 fuel was introduced in 2006. While ethanol blending remained around 1.53% until 2013-14, it has since increased progressively after the required production capacity, infrastructure and regulatory framework were put in place.Before the rollout of E20 in April 2026, extensive laboratory studies, durability trials and field validation were carried out to assess engine durability, material compatibility, fuel systems, corrosion resistance, drivability, emissions, fuel economy and overall vehicle performance.BS, or Bharat Stage, refers to India's vehicle emission standards, which prescribe limits for pollutants such as carbon monoxide (CO), nitrogen oxides (NOx), hydrocarbons (HC) and particulate matter (PM).
Article Summary: Road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari said tests found no issues in parameters such as drivability, startability, metal compatibility and plastic compatibility. The rollout of E20 petrol has faced criticism from opposition parties and some consumer groups. Opposition parties have repeatedly sought greater transparency on vehicle compatibility.

Article Title: Assam floods: Visuals show submerged villages, lakhs affected as death toll rises to 68
Article Text: GUWAHATI: Videos showing the impact of Assam's devastating floods are continuing to emerge as the state battles the aftermath of the deluge, with 5.24 lakh people across 763 villages still affected.Although the flood situation has started improving and waters are receding in several areas, the death toll has climbed to 68 after two more people died in Charaideo.The Dhansiri (South) at Numaligarh was the only river still flowing above the danger level.Nearly 48,742 hectares of crop area also remained submerged.Relief and rehabilitation efforts continued across the affected areas, with the state government also working to restore electricity in places where supply had been suspended as a precaution during the floods.The latest figures showed that the number of affected districts had fallen to nine, even as lakhs of people continued to deal with the impact of the floods.Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said state ministers would reach out across Assam to coordinate rehabilitation operations.The immediate priority, he said, remained providing relief to people in the worst-affected districts, including Sivasagar, Jorhat and Golaghat.The state government was also carrying out a coordinated exercise to restore power in flood-affected areas.Sarma said Assam Power Distribution Co Ltd teams were conducting safety inspections before restoring electricity in a phased manner across Sivasagar, Jorhat, Charaideo, Dhubri, Bongaigaon and other affected areas.The teams were working to restore essential services while ensuring that affected communities could return to normalcy, he said.As floodwaters receded in several areas, videos showing the impact of the deluge also continued to circulate online, giving a glimpse of the situation on the ground and the difficulties faced by people in affected areas.The latest situation comes as rescue, relief and rehabilitation efforts continue across the state.Union minister Sarbananda Sonowal on Sunday described the flood situation as "very serious", saying the Centre and the state government were working together on relief and rescue operations.Sonowal said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had been closely monitoring the situation since the floods began and had remained in touch with Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma.The NDRF and SDRF are continuing rescue and relief operations, while a high-level inter-ministerial team has arrived to speak to affected people and assess the situation.Singer Papon, who hails from Assam, has appealed to people in India and abroad to come forward and support those affected by the floods.In a video message, he spoke about villages being flooded, people remaining homeless and the loss of lives and animals.He urged people to look towards Assam and help in whatever way they could.
Article Summary: The death toll has climbed to 68 after two more people died in Charaideo. The Dhansiri (South) at Numaligarh was the only river still flowing above the danger level.Nearly 48,742 hectares of crop area also remained submerged.

Article Title: Weather tomorrow: IMD warns of heavy to very heavy rain across several states; Odisha, Chhattisgarh set for intense showers
Article Text:
Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are also expected in several regions.

NEW DELHI: Heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely to continue across several parts of the country on Tuesday, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issuing rain alerts for large parts of northwest, central, east, northeast and peninsular India.Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are also expected in several regions.Heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Delhi, Himachal Pradesh, Odisha, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Vidarbha.Heavy rainfall is also likely over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, coastal Andhra Pradesh, coastal Karnataka, East Rajasthan, Jammu and Kashmir, Jharkhand, Kerala, Mahe, Konkan, Goa, central Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, West Bengal and Sikkim.Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Andhra Pradesh, Gangetic West Bengal, central Maharashtra, Marathwada and north interior Karnataka.Similar conditions are also expected over Bihar, coastal Karnataka, East Rajasthan, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana.Delhi and adjoining areas are likely to witness heavy to very heavy rainfall, with thunderstorms and lightning also expected at isolated places.The IMD has advised people to remain alert as spells of intense rain may affect normal life.Heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Haryana, Delhi, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh.Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning are also likely over Uttarakhand and east Rajasthan.Odisha and Chhattisgarh are likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall, while heavy rain is also expected over Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Vidarbha.Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning are likely across several parts of the region.Heavy rainfall is likely over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, West Bengal and Sikkim.Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning are also expected over parts of the northeast.Konkan, Goa, Kerala, Mahe, coastal Karnataka, coastal Andhra Pradesh and central Maharashtra are likely to receive heavy rainfall.Thunderstorms with gusty winds are also forecast over north interior Karnataka, Marathwada, Telangana and parts of Andhra Pradesh.Hot and humid weather is likely to persist over coastal Andhra Pradesh.Widespread rainfall activity is likely to continue across large parts of northwest, central, eastern and peninsular India through August 1.Heavy rainfall is expected to persist over several states during the week, with isolated heavy to very heavy rainfall likely over parts of north, central and eastern India.
Article Summary: IMD issues rain alerts for large parts of northwest, central, east, northeast and peninsular India. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are also expected in several regions. Heavy to very heavy rainfall likely over Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Delhi, Himachal Pradesh, Odisha, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Vidarbha.

Article Title: UK company in spotlight as Nishikant Dubey vows 'disclosure' in Parliament
Article Text:
